result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): The two answers are close. Both explain why the scan passes, identify the div slots as the blocker, flag the aria-label mismatches with WCAG 2.5.3, and replace the green-border-only feedback with a role=status message. A's code is a little stronger: it uses a real form submit, moves focus to the problem field for both errors, and its success message reads naturally ('6:00 pm' rather than '18:00'). A is also more accurate in saying aria-labelledby on a role-less div 'isn't reliably exposed'; B says it is simply ignored. Neither answer explicitly says the label mismatch also affects screen-reader users, only voice-control users. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): The two answers are close: both name the div time slots as the blocker, move to native radios, remove the mismatched aria-labels and add a status region that announces the result. A marks the full slot as 'fully booked' in visible text, as the rubric asks. B hides that text with sr-only, though B does add focus management on errors and a real form submit. A also separates the blocking problems from the smaller label mismatches more clearly, so it edges ahead on matching the rubric.
